title: Reading the indentation: what runs when
idea: Indentation shows what is inside the loop vs inside the if vs after the loop.

exercises.prompt: A line indented under the if runs...
options: only when the if is true
exercises.explanation: Only when the if's condition is true, on the passes that match.

exercises.prompt: A line indented under the for but NOT under the if runs...
options: only when the if is true
exercises.explanation: Every pass of the loop — it is inside the loop but outside the if.
'pass' prints every pass (3 times); 'two!' prints only when i is 2. So pass, pass+two!, pass.

exercises.prompt: A line with NO indentation after the loop runs...
options: only when the if is true
exercises.explanation: Once, after the whole loop finishes — it is outside the loop entirely.

exercises.prompt: Deeper indentation means 'more inside' — inside the if, inside the loop.
exercises.explanation: True. Each indent level nests one layer deeper: loop, then if within it.

exercises.prompt: Match each indentation level to when its line runs.
exercises.explanation: Indent under for = every pass; indent under if = only when true; no indent after = once at the end.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: each pass print 'go', and when i is 3 also print 'hit'.
exercises.explanation: for header, then the every-pass print, then the if, then the if's print.
'go' is inside the loop but outside the if, so it prints every pass — four times.

exercises.prompt: How many times does 'hit' print in that same code?
exercises.explanation: 'hit' is under the if i == 3, true on only one pass, so it prints once.

exercises.prompt: Why does indentation matter so much here?
options: It decides what runs every pass vs only on matches
exercises.explanation: Indentation alone decides whether a line runs every pass, only on matches, or once at the end.
